_comment: Weekly snapshots of the OPEN CommitFest, used to compute week-over-week deltas. Only the current run's week and the previous week are kept in full (the previous one is needed for the delta and to track the fate of a patch flagged a week ago); every earlier week is collapsed to {week, cf, created_n, closed_n, net} in weeks_summary. Full history lives in references/archive/commitfest-2026.json (not read at runtime).

weeks_summary.net: in-window: 4 committed, 2 withdrawn; multiple new records (UUID cluster, reorder-buffer perf, ANALYZE sampling hook, new GUC/aggregate proposals)
5 created vs 27 closed in covered span -> net -22 (queue draining as In Progress began; commit tempo ~6x last week's 4)

weeks.highlight: Net +44 (64 created / 20 closed: 15 committed, 5 withdrawn, 0 rejected, 0 RwF) vs +10 last week; both weeks complete counts. The last week before PG20-3 closed to new entries produced the biggest intake since tracking began (64 vs the previous high of 46 on 10-12). Active PG20-3 queue 579 (415 NR / 48 WoA / 116 RfC) vs 535 (383/45/107). 13 RfC promotions (11 pre-existing, 2 brand-new: #7514 NOT-on-nullable-boolean selectivity, #7551 SSI write skew after summarization). 7 of the 15 commits closed entries filed this same week. One filer (shihao zhong) produced 9 entries, mostly BUG #-numbered fixes; Greg Burd filed 4 substantial internals patches (nbtree prefix compression #7523, hash-index metapage contention #7531, WAL CRC #7532, quickselect bounded sort #7565). Standout: #7523 nbtree opt-in leaf key prefix compression — URL index 22,177->7,506 pages (-66%) on inserts, WAL/txn 292->226 B, TPS within noise, point lookups unchanged but COUNT(*)/range scans +6-7% CPU from decoding; per-page opt-in format with no BTREE_VERSION bump. PG20-4 (#63) opened 11-01 with 2 entries.
